quest.title: Through the Gates of Ivory
quest.description: A lone lamp shines in the snowstorm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, this lamp is weird. But for some reason... now that we're near it, the blizzard's easing up. It even feels kind of warm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a minute. Paimon's heard that if you suddenly start feeling warm on a snowy mountain, it could mean you're so cold you're starting to hallucinate...

choices.text: Then I guess I'm hallucinating too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aha! So you felt it too! It really is getting warmer!
Don't worry, you two. This is a special lamp. They say it was blessed by the fae that is now inside it a long time ago.
It offers some protection from the cold.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! D—did someone just... appear out of nowhere?
Hello, my flying friend.
This is my lamp. I left it here earlier when I got a little bored and went for a walk.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so it's yours... Wait, you went for a walk in this blizzard? Dressed like that? How are you not freezing?
...Freezing?
Should I be reacting to temperature changes? Is that what you were expecting?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... That's not really the point. Most people would freeze solid if they wore that little in this weather like this.

choices.text: Maybe all the shivering is what keeps them from freezing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, because all that shivering would totally warm them up... As if! But that's only for regular people.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The fae don't really mind the cold. Just look at the Snegovik and the Jack Frosts. They probably don't do well in a place that's too warm.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But you don't look like a fae, and you're not cold either... So who are you, anyway? And what are you doing out here with no luggage and barely any warm clothes on?

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: I... I am Ikor. Someone... a woman told me to leave the house, but she didn't tell me where to go. So I've just been waiting here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The house...? You mean the House of Hesperides? We're on our way there for some wedding.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's never been to a Snegovik wedding before. They say the Snegovik live for love, right? So their weddings must be super romantic!

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: A wedding... Yes. For the Snegovik, it is an important <color=#00E1FFFF>ritual.</color> They have been preparing for it for a long time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So it must be a really big deal, right? Hehe, how exciting! Oh, right. Who's the woman you were talking about? You know, the one who told you to leave the house.

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: I have no idea. I'd never met her before that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: H—hold on! You mean to say that someone you didn't even know told you to leave the house, and you just went along with it!?

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: Yes. Because that was what she wanted, and she wanted it very badly. And if someone wanted something so badly that it becomes a wish, of course I should grant it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #({NICKNAME}... He doesn't look that young, but the way he talks and acts is just like a little child. He feels a little... not all there...)

response.speaker: Eye of Graeae
response.text: ...I can sense it. There's definitely a part of my body's power that's inside him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Wait, really? We found it already?)

response.speaker: Eye of Graeae
response.text: But the power inside him is incomplete. That may be why his mind seems a little... not quite there as well. The power that's in him... is so broken up that it's impossible to recover.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Then what do we do now?

response.speaker: Eye of Graeae
response.text: Before I can reclaim this part of my power, it must be restored to a more complete state first... I sense that the part of my body here was split up through a special ritual of some kind.

response.speaker: Eye of Graeae
response.text: If only I could get closer to the core of that power. Then I might be able to give you a clearer answer.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Sounds like we should head over to the wedding then.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (So are we taking him with us? Hmm... We can't just leave him here. But we still don't know why that person made him leave the house...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... This is kind of a strange favor to ask, but could you show us the way to the House of Hesperides?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We... don't really know the area, you see, and you're from there, so... you'd be the perfect guide!

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: Is this your wish?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes. Could you help me out with it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And Paimon thinks it'd be better for you, too! Even if you don't get cold, it just doesn't feel right for us to leave you out here in this storm dressed like that.

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: "People do not always know what is best for them. They choose storms in the morning, then pray for peace by night."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: Someone once told me that. While I do not feel the cold, maybe you are right.

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: So long as someone asks it of me, I am willing to grant their wish. Now, allow me to fulfill yours. Please follow me.

choices.text: I suppose there are some peoples who do fine in the cold?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, yeah! The fae don't really mind the cold. The Snegovik and Jack Frosts especially!

choices.text: Then we should probably keep telling ourselves we're freezing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... We're surrounded by snow and ice, and we still need to convince ourselves we're cold...?

talks.objective: Follow Ikor to the House of Hesperides

dialogues.text: Myshkin? Is that you? You're finally here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #...Huh? Who's Myshkin? No, we're just passing adventurers — {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We heard there was a wedding happening here, so we came by to take a look! And we do have an invite, so it's not like we're crashing the wedding, right?
Please present your invitation to the statue by the door.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The statue? Uh... okay, sure...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Ikor, you came from in there, right? Then you must know this place better than we do. Do they always have weird rules like this?)

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: (This does not seem to be part of the "ritual.")

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (So you're just as lost as we are. Well, since we're already here, let's just do what she said for now.)

dialogues.speaker: Saltykov
dialogues.text: The wedding is about to begin. We ask our guests to wait in the hall in the meantime...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's starting to feel a little nervous. It's like the Chicken-Mushroom Skewer she had this morning is dancing around in her stomach... Ugh.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wonders what Pavlina, the princess of the Snegurochka, is like... and what kind of person the groom is, too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If Aglaya's story is anything to go by, Pavlina sounds completely enchanted with him. Humans even tried to steal him away! He must be some kind of once-in-a-lifetime heartthrob.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: ...Maybe this wedding is more than it seems.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: #If what {NICKNAME} saw in the Pale Crown Palace really happened, then Pavlina was one of the people who betrayed Miss Aksinya... Which means...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pavlina probably has one of the pieces of your body.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: Right. The one who has the fragmented power of my body is... Ikor. So I suspect the groom may be...

dialogues.speaker: Enraptured Snegovik
dialogues.text: Pavlina! Pavlina!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Where did she come from?

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: She's the mistress of this place. A trick like that is child's play for her.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: But... no. How did she...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What have you found out?

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: Just as I expected. She carries a piece of my body's power in her life too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: Today is a special day. We were a people that no one ever blessed or cared for. But that changes now.

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: Love is what truly feeds the soul.

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: We were born without souls, so we chased after love because we longed to have one. We live for love, and we live because of love.

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: Yes. Human love is what gives us souls. It is what allows us to become beings in our own right.

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: But the humans who share their souls with us, they can be such terrible creditors who end up forcing us to live by the rules of their fickle love...

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: Larisa once stood here, too. You all saw the betrayal she suffered with your own eyes — vile enough to cost her both her soul and her life.

dialogues.speaker: Hesitant Snegovik
dialogues.text: But her death brought no shame upon us. On the contrary, it was something to be proud of, for it proved that nobility was always part of her nature.

dialogues.speaker: Rational Snegovik
dialogues.text: Nevertheless, her passing was a great loss to us, for there was no Snegurochka more pure-minded than Larisa.

dialogues.speaker: Rational Snegovik
dialogues.text: Pavlina, though... During her time at the Alypium — no, perhaps even before then... she had already been tainted by human ways.

dialogues.speaker: Rational Snegovik
dialogues.text: That would probably explain why she sees things this way. It is the sort of idea only a human could have, even if Pavlina herself does not realize it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Looks like not everyone agrees with her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, what Paimon really wants to know is, is that going to be your speech at the wedding? It sure doesn't sound like one...

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: ...Her wrongful death will be the final page in our kind's tragic chapter.

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: The new beginning granted to us by the gods shall soon arrive, and from this day forward, our soulless past shall finally come to an end.

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: You never knew the truth, and there is no need for you to know it now... For this day to come, a sacrifice had already been made some time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What's happening??? It feels like the air in the room has just changed all of a sudden...

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: Come to us, soul-water, born of the gods and made for the gods.

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: Come to us, Ikor. Come. Offer yourself up for our sake.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Wait, he's the groom? Hey! Ikor!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He can't seem to hear Paimon... What's wrong with him? Did someone do this to him? Or is it that shackle?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #We have to do something, {NICKNAME}! Paimon has a feeling this "ritual" isn't the wedding we thought it was going to be...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: No, it isn't. It is a ritual to transfer the power held in my body...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: However the Snegurochka princess came to possess that fragment of power before, she must have found a way to claim the rest of it now...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: She wants to defy the natural order and give those under her protection souls. But she would never be able to do that by herself alone. And that is where that power comes in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then we must do something now! She's going to take him!

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: Say it, Ikor. Do you promise to give us what we've been wishing for?

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: Yes, I do.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: I object to this union!

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: ...I know this is probably the last thing anyone wants to hear right now, but a Court Jester is supposed to speak up when advice is needed, isn't she?

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: ...Aksinya. Though I do not know how you managed to escape that inescapable prison... But you were not invited to today's proceedings.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: ...You never would have said that to me in the past, Pavlina.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: What changed you? Was it the pain of an ambition that could never be satisfied?

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: But you and I both know I have every right to be here — as an uninvited guest.

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: Stop it!

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: Why keep on fighting when you know it won't change anything? You know you won't win, not even now.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: I know. And that's why I came with some help this time.

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: A cheap little trick. All that will do is buy you a little time...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You simply do not understand, Aksinya. The sacrifice has already been made. That means the ending has already been set in motion, and there is nothing you can do to stop it.\nSo I failed this time. But what difference does it make? It's just one more "rehearsal"...\nNext time... Next time, it will work...

talks.objective: Hand over the invite by the statue

dialogues.speaker: Safonov
dialogues.text: The wedding is about to begin. We ask our guests to wait in the hall in the meantime...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Where did Ikor go? Goggles, did you see where he went?

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: My apologies. Some special ritual power seems to be affecting this entire place. I can no longer sense his presence. Given some time, I may be able to determine what's going on...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Honestly, Paimon still had so many questions for him. Like, if he's obviously just one part of one part of Goggles' body, how does he have a whole body of his own...?

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: That part is easy enough to understand. It is like... "A pomegranate split open, its seeds scattered across the ground. Piece the shell back together, and it can still, just barely, be called whole."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... Okay, even if he isn't really human, that example was still pretty creepy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But we're out of leads for now, so we'll just have to wait for Goggles to figure things out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Come on, {NICKNAME}, let's go soak up the wedding atmosphere! It's not every day you get to see a Snegovik wedding!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Looks like it's time! Everyone's heading toward the assembly hall.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We'd better catch up!

talks.objective: Go to the main hall for the wedding

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Where did Ikor go? Goggles, did you see where he went?

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: My apologies. Some special ritual power seems to be affecting this entire place. I can no longer sense his presence. Given some time, I may be able to determine what's going on...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Honestly, Paimon still had so many questions for him. Like, if he's obviously just one part of one part of Goggles' body, how does he have a whole body of his own...?

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: That part is easy enough to understand. It is like... "A pomegranate split open, its seeds scattered across the ground. Piece the shell back together, and it can still, just barely, be called whole."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... Okay, even if he isn't really human, that example was still pretty creepy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But we're out of leads for now, so we'll just have to wait for Goggles to figure things out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Come on, {NICKNAME}, let's go soak up the wedding atmosphere!

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: ...As far as I know, Pavlina, princess of the Snegurochka, isn't really the type to marry a human. How strange.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: If anything... I would have thought she'd be more attached to her own kind than to humans...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, you never know! Maybe she met the one and went, "Hehe, I don't care what anyone says! I'm marrying him!"

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: It's possible, but the chances are slim.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: Still... perhaps the wedding itself is the clue.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, then let's go to the wedding and see what we can find out! It's a Snegovik wedding, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #...{NICKNAME}... {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew — there you are! Did the bell wake you? You were completely out. Is the bed here really that comfy?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think I had a dream.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wonder. You were asleep for a long time. Paimon's been keeping watch the whole while. Was it a nice dream, or a scary one?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, never mind. Tell Paimon later. Now's not really the time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you remember what happened earlier? We came to the House of Hesperides for a wedding.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But that "ritual" wasn't a wedding at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That towering princess of the Snegurochka, Pavlina... She nearly killed Ikor...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon knows Ikor isn't really human, strictly speaking. He's just a fragment of the power that originally belonged to Goggles. But even so...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: Compassion is something to be respected, Miss Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thanks, Goggles. Oh, right, when Pavlina cast her spell, Goggles was the one who protected us and brought us here, somewhere safe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: While you were asleep, Paimon did some poking around. Looks like someone named Myshkin used to live here. Didn't Aglaya mention him when she first welcomed us?

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: ...*cough* Hello? Do you copy? You should be able to hear what I'm saying?

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: *sigh* Thanks for nothing, you two. I poured so much effort into getting "him" out, even if in part... Only for you to send him right back, as if nothing had happened. Pavlina almost won right there and then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Aksinya! Wait, how are you coming through Goggl—?

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: Ha! I am the creator of the Eye of Graeae, after all. I can still make use of some of its functions.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: ...Hmm. It's been a while since we last met, eh, dear colleague? Don't you think you're getting "a bit too passionate" right now?

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: Ah, sorry, that wasn't meant for you. I'm currently busy dealing with that crazy shrew... How tragic, Pavlina of the Snegovik. You've completely lost it.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: Her gaze is like Prime Ice, but her mind is like a powderkeg. A single spark could set her off and destroy all around her.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: I've trapped Pavlina, but have little time for anything else right now. Take "his" fragments away from here, one by one, while she's weakened by being in this area, away from her grasp.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: That's the only way to ensure that shrew won't be able to offer up "his" power for her people.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: We have to take back all that power, don't we? It's not the same as why she seeks your power, is it? "To have a body once more"... that's what you wish for, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: Y—Yes...

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: Then go. I won't be able to hold out for long... Hurry—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She's gone...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Take Goggles' fragments... one by one? What does she even mean? Doesn't she know that Pavlina has some of Goggles' power too???

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She may have something else up her sleeves too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... Better take what she says with a huge rock of salt. But what should we do now then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you know what? This is about Goggles! We should ask what he wants.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: I think... Maybe we should gather at least some of the power that has been split up, and try to make him as complete as possible. Then we can take it all back.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: This may sound a little ironic, but my wish is for the fragments, incomplete as they are, to be as whole as possible...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: It's just like how the Snegurochka princess must have decided to perform the ritual because she wanted to help her people become more "whole."

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: And that is something I can understand, and even empathize with, to some degree.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How can you feel for her!? She was gonna gobble you up, piece by piece, just to get what she wanted!!!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can share her food or Mora with other folks, no problem. But if you want Paimon to hand over an arm or a leg...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Or even Paimon's hair! Hmm... Actually, hair seems alright... especially if it's just a few strands—— Anyway, that's not the point.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It doesn't matter what the other person's reasons are. This is something... something Paimon needs to think over! Very carefully! Though Paimon probably won't say yes anyway, to be honest...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes. It's not good to over-deplete yourself for the sake of others.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: ...You are right. But that aside, there is another reason we must reclaim him "whole."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Another reason? And what would that be?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That you don't need to know, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Are the two of you keeping something from Paimon!? And Paimon's not talking about secret snack stashes or anything like tha——

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We should get moving.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: I have marked the fragment locations. Let's go, before the clock strikes ten.

dialogues.speaker: NPC#22708
dialogues.text: The "ritual" is already underway. Please go on in... There's no need to be anywhere else...

talks.objective: Get some rest before the wedding begins

dialogues.speaker: NPC#22709
dialogues.text: The "ritual" is already underway. Please go on in... There's no need to be anywhere else...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, you're already worn out? But what about the fun activities afterward...

choices.text: You're right. Let's go see what fun activities they've saved for after the main event.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: —Yay! —Mhm!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Exhaustion seems to have finally caught up with you. You and Paimon curl up together on the sofa, drifting into a light doze. Then, somewhere between sleep and waking, ten faint chimes ring out...

choices.text: That can wait. First, let's see the main course.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: All right, I'm with you.

talks.objective: Take a seat at the chapel

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That can wait. First, let's see the main course.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: All right, I'm with you.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Exhaustion seems to have finally caught up with you. You and Paimon curl up together on the sofa, drifting into a light doze. Then, somewhere between sleep and waking, eight faint chimes ring out...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's starting to feel a little nervous. It's like the Chicken-Mushroom Skewer she had this morning is dancing around in her stomach... Ugh.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wonders what Pavlina, the princess of the Snegurochka, is like... and what kind of person the groom is, too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If Aglaja's story is anything to go by, Pavlina sounds completely enchanted with him. Humans even tried to steal him away! He must be some kind of once-in-a-lifetime heartthrob.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! And then there's Ikor. He doesn't seem to be here either. Come to think of it, what was he doing in this mansion in the first place...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The princess of the Snegurochka has to be connected to all this somehow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon was thinking the same thing. But today's supposed to be a happy occasion, and everyone's here to offer her their blessings.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If we catch her in a good mood, maybe she'll let a clue or two slip.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: I have my doubts, Miss Paimon. Still, I agree. This is a good chance to gather clues up close.

dialogues.speaker: Enraptured Snegovik
dialogues.text: Pavlina! Pavlina!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Where did she come from?

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: She's the mistress of this place. A trick like that is child's play for her.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: But... no. How did she...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What have you found out?

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: I sense that she carries a piece of my body's power in her life too. How is that even possible?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: Today is a special day. We were a people that no one ever blessed or cared for. But that changes now.

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: Love is what truly feeds the soul.

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: We were born without souls, so we chased after love because we longed to have one. We live for love, and we live because of love.

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: Yes. Human love is what gives us souls. It is what allows us to become beings in our own right.

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: But the humans who share their souls with us, they can be such terrible creditors who end up forcing us to live by the rules of their fickle love...

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: Larisa once stood here, too. You all saw the betrayal she suffered with your own eyes — vile enough to cost her both her soul and her life.

dialogues.speaker: Hesitant Snegovik
dialogues.text: But her death brought no shame upon us. On the contrary, it was something to be proud of, for it proved that nobility was always part of her nature.

dialogues.speaker: Rational Snegovik
dialogues.text: Nevertheless, her passing was a great loss to us, for there was no Snegurochka more pure-minded than Larisa.

dialogues.speaker: Rational Snegovik
dialogues.text: Pavlina, though... During her time at the Alypium — no, perhaps even before then... she had already been tainted by human ways.

dialogues.speaker: Rational Snegovik
dialogues.text: That would probably explain why she sees things this way. It is the sort of idea only a human could have, even if Pavlina herself does not realize it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Looks like not everyone agrees with her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, what Paimon really wants to know is, is that going to be your speech at the wedding? It sure doesn't sound like one...

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: ...Her wrongful death will be the final page in our kind's tragic chapter.

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: The new beginning granted to us by the gods shall soon arrive, and from this day forward, our soulless past shall finally come to an end.

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: You never knew the truth, and there is no need for you to know it now... For this day to come, a sacrifice had already been made some time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What's happening??? It feels like the air in the room has just changed all of a sudden...

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: Come to us, soul-water, born of the gods and made for the gods.

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: Come to us, Ikor. Come. Offer yourself up for our sake.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Wait, he's the groom? Hey! Ikor!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He can't seem to hear Paimon... What's wrong with him? Did someone do this to him? Or is it that shackle?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #We have to do something, {NICKNAME}! Paimon has a feeling this "ritual" isn't the wedding we thought it was going to be...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: I'm afraid you're right.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: However the Snegurochka princess came to possess that fragment of power before, she must have found a way to claim the rest of it now...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: She wants to defy the natural order and give those under her protection souls. But she would never be able to do that by herself alone. And that is where that power comes in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then we must do something now! She's going to take him!

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: Say it, Ikor. Do you promise to give us what we've been wishing for?

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: Yes, I do.
I object to this union!
...I know this is probably the last thing anyone wants to hear right now, but a Court Jester is supposed to speak up when advice is needed, isn't she?

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: ...Aksinya. Though I do not know how you managed to escape that inescapable prison... But you were not invited to today's proceedings.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: Yes, yes, you already told me that earlier today. With not a trace of kindness left for an old colleague. How sad.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: But you and I both know I have every right to be here — as an uninvited guest.

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: Stop it!

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: Why keep on fighting when you know it won't change anything? You know you won't win, not even now.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: I know. And that's why I came with some help this time.

dialogues.speaker: Pavlina
dialogues.text: A cheap little trick. All that will do is buy you a little time...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You simply do not understand, Aksinya. The sacrifice has already been made. That means the ending has already been set in motion, and there is nothing you can do to stop it.\nSo I failed this time. But what difference does it make? It's just one more "rehearsal"...\nNext time... Next time, it will work...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
"The clock strikes again."
A cold voice whispers the words in your ear. You know this isn't the first time you've heard something like this before.
In that voice, you hear a soul taking shape, polished by countless trials until it slowly grows to be more beautiful. That is, if pain, too, could be called beautiful...
In that same voice, you hear a soul taking form, growing ever more magnificent as it undergoes an endless process of transcendence. That is, if distortion, too, could be called magnificent...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
Each time brings greater pain than the last.
Each time brings you closer to the thing you've been longing for...
And yet...
The mouth opens, then slowly closes again. It is too late. No words can stop what has already begun.
After all, that wish matters more than anything now.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
"Yes. The clock strikes again. So let us begin once more. Your..."
You say you know you've heard these words before...
"Mine."\nn"'Ours...'"
"This endless 'wedding' of ours."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Should we wait here until the wedding starts?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Exhaustion seems to have finally caught up with you. You and Paimon curl up together on the sofa, drifting into a light doze. Then, somewhere between sleep and waking, eight faint chimes ring out...

choices.text: Hold on. There are still a few things we need to do.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Then we'd better hurry! We don't want to be late to a wedding.

dialogues.text: Welcome to the House of Hesperides.

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: Since you have an invitation, then you are guests of this house, and every guest deserves a proper welcome. You may call me Aglaya.

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: Is this your first time attending a Snegovik wedding?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mmhmm

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: You two do not seem to be from around here, so I take it you have not heard about the scandal. I doubt you would have been willing to come here if you had.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A scandal?

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: At least, humans would call it that. The last ceremonial ritual we held on this scale was Larisa's wedding.

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: But that human betrayed her in the end. She killed him, and then the vow took her life, too.

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: Larisa was the most beautiful of us all... even the way she died was beautiful.

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: That day, her fury brought down a blizzard so fierce, it froze even the bolts of lightning mid-fall. You should have seen that beautiful, deadly Prime Ice magic...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Umm...

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: Heh, but you have no cause for worry. You will be safe here at the House of Hesperides, as long as you stay away from what is forbidden.

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: The ritual will begin when <color=#00E1FFFF>the clock strikes eight times</color>. Please make your way to the chapel right away when you hear it.

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: Until then, you may look around the main hall... The other rooms are not open to guests...

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: But you are welcome to enjoy the entertainment here, or simply rest for a while. The choice is yours.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, about those rooms we're not allowed into...

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: Some of those are private quarters. We even have one set aside for the bride and groom...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ah, excuse. I didn't mean to be rude.

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: Once, there was a human woman who dared sneak into the groom's room while he was alone. Of course, she was caught almost immediately...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh-what!? Was she trying to steal the groom or something???

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: Not from Pavlina, the Snegurochka princess. What Pavlina has laid claim to, no one takes from her.

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: So cold is she by nature, she hardly seems like a Snegurochka at all. But that boy was hers, and there was no way she would let anyone take him away.

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: ...Regardless of that, the ritual will go ahead, and we will succeed this time. She has sworn it on the sword Larisa once wielded.

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: And we all know what happens to those who break their vows.

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: Enough of the dull introductions. This ritual is one that is worth celebrating after all. I wish the both of you a most pleasant and unforgettable day here at the House of Hesperides.

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: Oh my, you ended up all the way over here?

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: Let's get you back where you're supposed to be.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, you're already worn out? But what about the fun activities afterward...

choices.text: That can wait. First, let's see the main course.
You're right. Let's go see what fun activities they've saved for after the main event.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that's awesome

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's starting to feel a little nervous. It's like the Chicken-Mushroom Skewer she had this morning is dancing around in her stomach... Ugh.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wonders what Pavlina, the princess of the Snegurochka, is like... and what kind of person the groom is, too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If Aglaya's story is anything to go by, Pavlina sounds completely enchanted with him. Humans even tried to steal him away! He must be some kind of once-in-a-lifetime heartthrob.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: ...Maybe this wedding is more than it seems.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: #If what {NICKNAME} saw in the Pale Crown Palace really happened, then Pavlina was one of the people who betrayed Miss Aksinya... Which means...

dialogues.text: Pavlina probably has one of the pieces of your body.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, this lamp is weird. But for some reason... now that we're near it, the blizzard's easing up. It even feels kind of warm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a minute. Paimon's heard that if you suddenly start feeling warm on a snowy mountain, it could mean you're so cold you're starting to hallucinate...

choices.text: Then I guess I'm hallucinating too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aha! So you felt it too! It really is getting warmer!
Don't worry, you two. This is a special lamp. They say it was blessed by the fae that is now inside it a long time ago.
It offers some protection from the cold.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! D—did someone just... appear out of nowhere?
Hello, you two. Don't be so alarmed, my flying friend.
This is my lamp. I left it here earlier when I got a little bored and went for a walk.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so it's yours... Wait, you went for a walk in this blizzard? Dressed like that? How are you not freezing?
...Freezing?
Should I be reacting to temperature changes? Is that what you were expecting?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... That's not really the point. Most people would freeze solid if they wore that little in this weather like this.

choices.text: Maybe all the shivering is what keeps them from freezing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, because all that shivering would totally warm them up... As if! But that's only for regular people.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The fae don't really mind the cold. Just look at the Snegovik and the Jack Frosts. They probably don't do well in a place that's too warm.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But you don't look like a fae, and you're not cold either... So who are you, anyway? And what are you doing out here with no luggage and barely any warm clothes on?

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: I... I am Ikor. Someone... a woman told me to leave the house, but she didn't tell me where to go. So I've just been waiting here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A house...? You mean there's a house up here on this snowy mountain? With people living in it?

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: Yes, there is a house. It is called the House of Hesperides, and it is where the Snegovik live. The lady of the house is Pavlina, the Snegurochka princess.

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: Right now... I believe she is preparing for her wedding.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A Snegovik wedding?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's never been to a Snegovik wedding before. They say the Snegovik live for love, right? So their weddings must be super romantic!

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: A wedding... Yes. For the Snegovik, it is an important <color=#00E1FFFF>ritual.</color> They have been preparing for it for a long time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So it must be a really big deal, right? Hehe, how exciting! Hmm... Do you think we can go see it?

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: Is that what you wish for?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, with the storm this bad, it'd be nice to have somewhere to rest for a bit... And besides, we'd get to see a Snegovik wedding...

choices.text: So this is Paimon's wish, then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, yeah!

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: I understand. In that case, please take this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, what's that?

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: This is a wedding invitation. With it, the house will receive you... as honored guests of the ritual.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But um... isn't this invite yours?

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: No... friend who is named Paimon. Invitations are only for guests.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, okay! Thank you then! Oh, right... Who's the woman you were talking about? You know, the one who told you to leave the house.

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: I have no idea. I'd never met her before that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: H—hold on! You mean to say that someone you didn't even know told you to leave the house, and you just went along with it!?

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: Yes. Because that was what she wanted, and she wanted it very badly. And if someone wanted something so badly that it becomes a wish, of course I should grant it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #({NICKNAME}... He doesn't look that young, but the way he talks and acts is just like a little child. He feels a little... not all there...)

response.speaker: Eye of Graeae
response.text: ...I can sense it. There's definitely a part of my body's power that's inside him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Wait, really? We found it already?)

response.speaker: Eye of Graeae
response.text: But the power inside him is incomplete. That may be why his mind seems a little... not quite there as well. The power that's in him... is so broken up that it's impossible to recover.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Then what do we do now?

response.speaker: Eye of Graeae
response.text: Before I can reclaim this part of my power, it must be restored to a more complete state first... I sense that the part of my body here was split up through a special ritual of some kind.

response.speaker: Eye of Graeae
response.text: If only I could get closer to the core of that power. Then I might be able to give you a clearer answer.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Sounds like we should head over to the wedding then.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (So are we taking him with us? Hmm... We can't just leave him here. But we still don't know why that person made him leave the house...)

response.speaker: Paimon

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We... don't really know the area, you see, and you're from there, so... you'd be the perfect guide!

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: Is this your wish?

response.speaker: Player

response.speaker: Paimon

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: "People do not always know what is best for them. They choose storms in the morning, then pray for peace by night."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: Someone once told me that. While I do not feel the cold, maybe you are right.

response.speaker: Ikor
response.text: So long as someone asks it of me, I am willing to grant their wish. Now, allow me to fulfill yours. Please follow me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, you are the best!

choices.text: Then we should probably keep telling ourselves we're freezing...

response.speaker: Paimon

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What's this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... So the wedding is being held at... House of Hesp-something, up on the snowy mountain...

dialogues.text: House of Hesperides. Yes. It was once home to the sovereign who ruled over the Snegovik. As for Pavlina...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: That name does sound faintly familiar...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, Pavlina, the princess of the Snegurochka, might be tied to Goggles' past too?

dialogues.text: Most likely.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The house's all the way up the mountain? And we still have to climb higher?

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae

dialogues.speaker: Paimon

dialogues.text: The house is just past the bridge.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, it's really lively here... Is this part of the activities that Snegurochka mentioned?

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: Stay close, I'll light the lamp for you. There's nothing to fear.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Come on, let's go take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's try knocking first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #The bell's ringing again. But why? Paimon has a really bad feeling about this... {NICKNAME}, we need to hurry...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like all the wedding guests are Snegovik...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, are we even supposed to be here? And Ikor's nowhere to be seen either...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Goggles, you said he was part of your power, didn't you? So when you get your body back, will you look like him too?

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: I cannot say for certain, but it is possible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hmm... Don't worry, {NICKNAME}! Even if Goggles ends up being super good-looking, Paimon's still your number one guide!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like all the wedding guests are Snegovik...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now that Paimon thinks about it, Anka from that mumbly-jumbly town kind of looked like him too.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: I cannot say for certain, but it is possible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hmm... Don't worry, {NICKNAME}! Even if Goggles ends up being super good-looking, Paimon's still your number one guide!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, Pavlina, princess of the Snegurochka... Paimon feels like that name's come up before...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: #The Pale Crown Palace... {NICKNAME} told us about the past {M#he}{F#she} saw in the Shadow Realm.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: Pavlina... Yes. She was one of the great ones who presided over the Alypium — princess of the Snegovik clan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so that's who she was... And that Ikor felt kind of off, too...
